_comment: Playable eras. Each has its own trained model, its own player pool, and its own OVRs derived by simulating players through that era's model (ml/train/derive_ovr.py) rather than by any hand-written formula. Boundaries sit where the scoring data actually breaks -- runs/ball jumps +0.080 at 2013->2014 and +0.070/+0.095 at 2022->2023 (see ml/etl/season_shift.py). Seasons are calendar years taken from match dates, NOT the ambiguous Cricsheet `season` label.
_cutoffs: min_bat_balls / min_bowl_balls decide whether a player is RATEABLE in an era, not whether the auction can be filled -- every era supplies 200+ draftable players against the 175 an 8-team auction needs. Below these counts a rating is mostly noise.

eras.label: Genesis
eras.tagline: Petrol ₹45 a litre, 7.84 an over. Both a bargain — and a six was still an event.

eras.label: The Shift
eras.tagline: Petrol doubles past ₹90. The rate crawls to 8.36. Bats get bigger, so does the bill.

eras.label: Modern Era
eras.tagline: Petrol ₹95 and 9.51 an over. Runs are the last thing in India still going cheap.

eras.label: Multiverse
eras.tagline: 2011 Gayle at ₹45 a litre meets 2024 Gayle at ₹95. Same man, very different economy.
eras._note: Pool built by ml/etl/multiverse.py: each era's version of a player as a separate, era-tagged entry. A ball can pair a 2009 batter with a 2025 bowler, so one model has to resolve it -- the MIDDLE era, since it sits between the other two and neither end is played under wholly foreign rules. Players keep their own era's stats, which the model reads as inputs, so each version still behaves like himself. Every tagged name is a stranger to that model, and cold_effect (E = A.W) is what stops them all collapsing to an identical league-average player.

eras.label: All-Time Legends
eras.tagline: Nineteen years: the run rate up 21%, petrol up 111%. Everyone who ever played.
eras._note: Deliberately NOT the learned engine. This is the nostalgia mode: the original hand-tuned pipeline with the original career OVRs, where Gayle is a 93 because of what he did, not what he would do against 2026 bowling. Uses data/players_historical.json unchanged.
